Testimony in Support of LD 1649 - Resolve, to Establish the Blue Ribbon Commission to Study the Operations of the Legislature and LD 1673 - Resolve, to Establish a Pilot Project to Facilitate the Inclusion of Economic Impact Statements in the Legislative Process Catherine Robbins-Halsted Co-owner Robbins Lumber, Inc.
Chairpersons, Members of the Committee:
Thank you for the opportunity to provide written testimony in support of LD 1649 and LD 1673. My name is Catherine Robbins-Halsted, and I own and operate a small sawmill in Maine that employs 200 hardworking people. I'm here not just as a business owner, but as a lifelong Mainer deeply invested in the economic future of our state.
Maine has long suffered from short-term, fragmented policymaking. For years, we've seen legislation debated and passed without a clear sense of its long-term consequences or how it fits into any larger economic vision. We don't consistently ask how a bill contributes to better jobs, more innovation, or stronger communities. We don't ask how it affects our workforce, our tax base, or our kids' chances of building lives here. Too often, we vote in isolation--without a strategy, without research, and without context.
The result? One disconnected decision after another has led to what we're seeing today. Maine consistently ranks near the bottom in national economic indicators. Dozens of successful, homegrown Maine companies have been sold to out-of-state owners. We're losing young people, struggling to attract investment, and watching communities hollow out.
LD 1673, with bipartisan sponsorship, offers a small but powerful step in the right direction. It proposes a pilot project to begin including economic impact statements in the legislative process. In other words, it asks: Before we pass a law, what will it do to our economy? How will it help--or hurt--our long-term goals for productivity, competitiveness, and prosperity?
As a small business owner, I make decisions every day based on long-term planning, risk analysis, and the health of my workforce. I can't afford to guess or hope things will work out. I need data. I need strategy. And I believe the same should be expected of our lawmakers.
LD 1673 will help us get there. It doesn't mandate outcomes--it simply provides information. Information that can help us build a more coordinated, thoughtful approach to legislation that actually grows Maine's economy and supports working families.

And LD 1649 is just as important. A Blue Ribbon Commission focused on studying how the Legislature operates--and how it might function more strategically--is long overdue. If we want better outcomes for our people, we need to be honest about the process and committed to improving it.
The future of Maine depends on our willingness to be smarter, more strategic, and more forward-thinking. These two bills won't solve every problem overnight--but they're a meaningful and necessary start.
Please support LD 1649 and LD 1673.
Thank you.
10049822:
James Lynch BREWER LD 1649
Please approve LD 1649, our current legislative process needs to be reviewed. We look at over 2000 bills every year in isolation from each other, with no strategic plan or direction. Members of the public should be able to comment on and have a voice concerning how their Legislature operates. The Legislature works for the people, not the other way around. It is a public service and the public should very much have a say in how it operates. LD 1649 has bipartisan sponsorship and seeks to provide information on ways to modernize and improve efficiency and effectiveness of the Maine Legislature.

TESTIMONY OF
Joel Allumbaugh, President & Chief Executive Officer
The Allumbaugh Agency
Before the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government
May 5, 2025
L.D. 1649 "Resolve, to Establish the Blue Ribbon Commission to Study the Operations of
the Legislature"
Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government. My name is Joel Allumbaugh; I am the President & Chief Executive Officer of the Allumbaugh Agency, a full-service employee benefit agency specializing in the design and administration of employee benefit plans. Our customers are Maine small businesses and their employees. I also serve as a Board Member of the Maine Jobs Council. I appreciate the opportunity to provide this testimony in support of LD 1649, Resolve, to Establish the Blue Ribbon Commission to Study the Operations of the Legislature.
I have worked across both the public and private sectors in Maine - as a small business owner, a health policy advocate, and as someone deeply committed to improving how we develop and implement public policy in this state. As such, I have witnessed firsthand the long-term challenges Maine is facing: an aging population, a shrinking workforce, and economic and demographic rankings that lag behind most of the nation. If we are going to reverse those trends, modernizing and improving the efficiency and effectiveness of the way we govern is just as important as the policies we pass.
The Legislature today is asked to address increasingly complex issues with limited time, support, and sometimes outdated institutional processes. The way we currently operate often leaves little room for proactive, data-driven policymaking. In many cases, lawmakers are forced to react to problems rather than prevent them.
We need a legislature that is better equipped to make long-term, strategic decisions. That means reviewing structural inefficiencies here in Maine, studying what is working in other states, and making evidence-based recommendations for reform. Whether it's evaluating the overall structure of the legislature, improving access to nonpartisan research and analysis, or using modern technology to streamline communication and collaboration--there is no shortage of opportunities to improve.
As President & Chief Executive Officer of the Allumbaugh Agency and a Board Member of the Maine Jobs Council, I know firsthand how better infrastructure--whether in health data or economic policy--can lead to better outcomes. The same holds true for how the legislature functions.

This bill is not about partisanship or process for its own sake. It's about ensuring that the Maine Legislature is equipped to meet the challenges of the 21st century, serving the people efficiently and effectively, and enabling a more prosperous future for our state.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely,
Joel Allumbaugh

Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government:
My name is Mike Roughton and I am submitting this testimony on behalf of the Manufacturers Association of Maine in strong support of LD 1649, Resolve, to Establish the Blue Ribbon Commission to Study the Operations of the Legislature. The Manufacturers Association of Maine (MAME) is a non-partisan 501(c)6 nonprofit grounded in service to its membership, providing a network of resources designed to support the strategic business growth needs of Maine manufacturing entrepreneurs. Maine's manufacturing businesses are diverse, employing almost 60,000 individuals in military and defense, aerospace, metal fabrication, paper, boat building, semi-conductor, wood products, aquaculture and biotech, medical device, composites, and bioplastics, as well as the food and beverage industries. These businesses represent almost 10% of Maine's annual GDP and 14.5% of all the wages paid in the state on a weekly basis. MAME's mission is to help manufacturing grow and succeed and supports Maine's development of future manufacturing assets through a variety of programs. The necessity for this commission is underscored by the pressing need for the Legislature to function effectively and efficiently in serving the citizens of our great state...
Meetings held last fall by the Rules Committee had stakeholder's hoping that significant changes would be made to the legislative process. Countless stakeholders with diverse backgrounds and experience(including MAME and its representatives) weighed-in, raising concerns about transparency, accountability, civility and time management. The conversations were robust, and many believed the process would lead to meaningful changes. Unfortunately, the reforms ultimately adopted by the 132nd Legislature have done little to address those concerns.
The health, safety, and welfare of Maine's communities, its citizens and the nonprofits and businesses who operate here depend on a responsive and adaptive legislative body that can meet the challenges of an ever-evolving political and social landscape. The proposed commission aims to examine the existing structure and operations of the Legislature, ensuring that it can effectively address the needs of those constituencies.
By convening this Commission, the legislature would position itself to gain valuable insights and implement necessary changes in a timely manner. This

until 90 days after adjourmnent unless enacted as emergencies; and
